name: Cat-cow
why: Moves your whole spine gently through rounding and arching. It eases stiffness and is a kind first exercise when the back is sore or after a run.
setup: Get on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
cues: Then lift your chest and tailbone
mistakes: Forcing the end of the range
feel: Gentle movement and stretch along the back.
stopIf: Pain shoots into your leg, or one direction clearly makes the pain worse. Then stay in the comfortable range.

name: Bird dog
why: Trains the trunk muscles to keep your spine steady while your arms and legs move: the kind of endurance that protects the back when running and lifting. One of McGill's 'big 3' back exercises.
setup: Get on hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat.
cues: Reach opposite arm and leg out long
Keep your back still as a tabletop
mistakes: Lifting the leg too high and arching the back
Letting the hips tip to one side
feel: Effort in the back of the hip, along the back and around the trunk.
stopIf: Sharp back pain, or pain spreading down your leg.
references: McGill SM. Low Back Disorders: Evidence-Based Prevention and Rehabilitation. Human Kinetics.

name: Glute bridge
why: Strengthens the glutes, which share the load with your lower back and knees when you run, climb stairs and lift.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, arms by your sides.
cues: Squeeze your glutes, then lift your hips
Straight line from knees to shoulders
mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels
Feeling it mostly in the hamstrings (bring your heels a little closer)
feel: Your glutes working. A little in the back of the thighs is fine.
stopIf: Lower-back pain increases during the exercise.
